stories.headline: Sean Payton says he's taking over playcalling for Broncos' offense
stories.summary: Broncos coach Sean Payton said Thursday he is taking over the offensive playcalling beginning Sunday against the Chargers as the team looks to kick-start a sputtering offense.
stories.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton said Thursday he is taking over the offensive playcalling beginning Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers as the team looks to kick-start a sputtering offense.

"We'll make a change offensively. I'll call the plays," Payton told reporters Thursday.

Payton had surrendered the playcalling duties to first-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb during the offseason.

"I've done this long enough where I know when I have a future head coach. And he's going to be one," Payton said of Webb.

Payton has repeatedly said in recent weeks he's been frustrated with the team's lack of consistency in the run game as well as their difficulties on first down that has consistently put the offense in difficult down-and-distance situations.

The Broncos (2-2) are near the bottom of the league rankings in scoring (27th), total yards per game (27th), rushing yards per game (29th), passing yards per game (20th), QBR (23rd) and Offensive EPA (22nd at -7.48). Only six teams have had more three-and-out possessions than the Broncos this season as 27.5% of their possessions have ended with three plays and a punt.

Quarterback Bo Nix is also currently ranked 22nd in QBR (46.1) and 27th in average air yards per attempt (5.9) as the lack of big plays on offense has become a four-game trend. The Broncos, overall, are 29th in the league in plays of 20 or more yards and 30th in explosive plays with 16 (runs of at least 10 yards and pass plays of at least 20 yards).

Payton said Wednesday he believes it all tracks to "the details, the little things,'' rather than some substantial shift in approach on offense as the team prepares to face the Chargers (0-4) Sunday in SoFi Stadium.

"The inconsistencies, the details, the little things,'' Payton said Wednesday. "... Let's focus on the attention to detail and the rest will follow.''

stories.headline: Scoring way up to start 2026-27 after shorter preseason
stories.summary: The first three days of the earliest leaguewide start in NHL history delivered scores straight out of the 1980s.
stories.body:
The first three days of the earliest leaguewide start in NHL history delivered scores straight out of the 1980s.

Edmonton and Vancouver played 6-5 and 9-7 games. Pittsburgh routed Philadelphia 7-0. Colorado beat Los Angeles 8-4.

"There's a lot of goals being scored, which tells you that there's some loose hockey still being played," New York Islanders coach Peter DeBoer said Thursday.

The hockey has been sloppy, scoring is up slightly, and goaltenders are stopping the puck less than last season. But with the first 100 or so games in the books following shorter training camps and less exhibition action, there's little evidence to suggest that it has drastically altered the play on the ice compared to previous starts that come with gaps in fundamentals and the occasional blowout.

"I think it's been like that for the last 100 years, so I was not expecting this year to be any different," Utah Mammoth coach Andre Tourigny said.

The first 110 games have featured 344 goals -- led by Oilers defenseman Evan Bouchard with six. New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin even has one from shooting and scoring into an empty net.

That's an average of 6.26 per game, up a tick from the 6.1 over the first 112 games a year ago. Power plays are clicking at a 20.9% success rate, compared to 19.8%, led by Tourigny's Mammoth at 61.5%.

"Maybe less time to practice special teams," said Utah's Dylan Guenther, who leads the league with six power-play points. "We had a pretty big emphasis on that in camp because we did a lot of special teams, so it's good that a little bit of that is paying off."

The average save percentage is .890. Netminders combining for an .896 last season was the lowest in the NHL since 1994, and it's not getting any easier for hockey's masked men.

There are a similar amount of giveaways, more than 16 per game, and plenty of odd-man rushes to be found.

"Teams can score, like there's so much skill," New Jersey Devils defenseman Brenden Dillon said. "Teams have so much skill, so on the defensive side, all it takes is one stick being in the wrong spot or one guy being out of position and teams are going to make you pay."

It is an annual debate every fall how to get the most out of camp, Devils coach Sheldon Keefe said, which leads to plenty of teaching early in the regular season.

"Do we roll out everything and then introduce it, but then you don't get good at anything?" Keefe said. "Or do you just roll out a few things at a time and try to really grasp onto that and then you build out from there? You have to do that even more so in the shortened camp. You've got to kind of prioritize a few key areas you focus on, and then you just keep kind of building it out as you go."

Player fitness is not a concern in this day and age when summer skates are commonplace. It may take several more weeks to determine if fewer preseason games contributed to any sort of increase in injuries.

More games are slipping away from teams with big deficits, though. There have been 22 decided by three or more goals, a little more than usual.

"Everybody's pretty sharp pretty early," Islanders captain Bo Horvat said. "You get the odd game here and there where it gets a little sloppy. But I think obviously play will pick up and things will get a little bit crispier as the season goes on."

Teammate Kyle Palmieri said the Islanders discussed taking advantage of some of the sloppiness around the league, hoping that being more disciplined in the fall can pay dividends. Dillon understands coaches probably would have liked another week or two to iron some things out, but there isn't much clamoring to go back to the old ways.

"It's nice having a shorter camp," Guenther said. "I'm not going to complain about that."

Good thing, then, because this is the NHL's new normal. As part of that, everyone seems to acknowledge this is how early-season fall hockey goes -- a long way from playoff races in the spring and the lockdown, tight-checking intensity chasing the Stanley Cup.

"I think there's a lot of clean up to do from everybody," Tourigny said. "At this point, I don't think there's any team who's perfectly perfect on anything."

stories.headline: Sources: 76ers plan to play starters in preseason game vs. Nets
stories.summary: The 76ers plan to play their starters Thursday against the Nets, sources told ESPN.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- The Philadelphia 76ers plan to play their starters Thursday against the Brooklyn Nets, sources told ESPN, giving fans a first preseason glimpse of LeBron James in a Sixers uniform.

Sixers coach Nick Nurse told reporters that if all of his main players came through Wednesday's practice healthy, he hoped to play "the majority" of them -- namely James, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe -- together in the first half against the Nets.

James, Embiid and Maxey were healthy scratches in Philadelphia's preseason-opening victory Monday against the New York Knicks.

Brown scored 22 points in 17 minutes Monday while Edgecombe had 12 points and seven assists in 20 minutes.

stories.headline: MLB division series 2026: Lineups, keys for ALDS Game 4
stories.summary: Cleveland rebounded to avoid being swept. Can it force a Game 5 or will the White Sox advance to face Tampa Bay in the ALCS?
stories.body:
We've got a Game 4 in the American League Division Series.

The Cleveland Guardians rode a four-run third inning to victory over the Chicago White Sox to stave off elimination in Game 3. Will the Guardians be able to replicate that success Thursday to force a decisive Game 5 in Cleveland? Or will the White Sox finish business in front of their home crowd and advance to face the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL Championship Series?

We'll have all the day's action covered -- from lineups and keys to the game before first pitch to in-game analysis and postgame takeaways.

Key links: Mega-preview | Series outlooks | Bracket | Schedule

Cleveland Guardians at Chicago White Sox (8 p.m. ET)
White Sox lead series 2-1

Starting pitchers: Parker Messick vs. Hagen Smith

How the Guardians can even the series: Cleveland needs a midseason-type start from Parker Messick. He was just OK in his Game 1 outing against the White Sox, lasting only 4⅓ innings. The Guardians probably will need more from him in Game 4 after using seven pitchers to get through Game 3, including closer Cade Smith for two innings. Of course, it wouldn't hurt if veteran slugger Jose Ramirez had another all-world game -- he was fantastic in Wednesday's win to stave off elimination. He and Messick can force a Game 5 by themselves. -- Jesse Rogers

The Guardians have to feel pretty good about their position, at least as good as a team can be one loss away from elimination. They aren't likely to repeat their Game 3 combo -- 19 strikeouts by the pitchers, 10 walks by the batters -- but a lesser variation of that formula will still play. The White Sox have been resilient this season, so Cleveland will want to strike early to keep the momentum that was so electric early Wednesday cooking all through the game. If that happens, the Guardians' hitters can stay patient and their pitchers can attack a possibly anxious White Sox lineup, much like what happened Wednesday. -- Bradford Doolittle

stories.headline: Jake Paul cleared to fight; Canelo, Strickland, others on wish list
stories.summary: Jake Paul, who has been cleared to resume fighting after recovering from a broken jaw, has a list of big names he'd like to face in boxing and MMA now that he's back.
stories.body:
Jake Paul has been medically cleared to return to boxing.

Paul (12-2, seven KOs), 29, has not fought since he suffered a broken jaw during his knockout loss to Anthony Joshua last December. Paul underwent surgical procedures on his jaw in December and February. Nakisa Bidarian, co-founder of Paul's Most Valuable Promotions, officially updated Paul's status Thursday.

"Jake Paul has been cleared to return to the boxing ring," Bidarian wrote on X.

Paul told ESPN in April that he'd resumed light training but had not been cleared to spar. He has targeted a full return to competition in early 2027.

In connection to the update on his health, Paul provided his latest wish list of eventual fights this week. The list included 15 potential fights, including Canelo Alvarez, Ryan Garcia, Francis Ngannou, Deontay Wilder in boxing as well as mixed martial arts contests against Conor McGregor and Nate Diaz.

The list also included UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland (31-7), who linked himself to Paul this week in a series of online posts expressing frustration about his UFC contract.

"I gotta be honest, unless things change with the UFC I'm kinda over it," Strickland wrote on X. "McGregor makes 30 million to fight for 30 seconds and they don't want to pay us a fraction of it. Contemplating just going to 205 [pounds], knocking out my contract and scrapping with [Jake Paul]. That sounds fun."

Paul, who has been vocal for years along with MVP in encouraging the UFC to increase its fighter pay, acknowledged Strickland's post in a response.

"Sean Strickland I see your texts but are you out of contract?" Paul wrote. "Tell your 'promoter' to call MVP."

stories.headline: Fever's Clark denounces online hate directed at 'good soul' Mitchell
stories.summary: Caitlin Clark said she has talked with Kelsey Mitchell since her teammate spoke about online hate she has received and the difficulty of playing with the Fever.
stories.body:
Caitlin Clark held her final media session of the season Thursday and said she has talked with Kelsey Mitchell since her backcourt mate spoke about online hate she has received and the difficulty of playing with the Indiana Fever at times.

The intense attention the organization has gotten since Clark joined has attracted a vocal group that has been abusive to Fever players and others around the league.

"Showing up every day to compete for fans that may or may not like you is hard," Mitchell had said Saturday during her season-ending media session.

It "makes you upset," Clark said of what her teammate has gone through, noting that Mitchell is a "good soul." Clark denounced anyone who would spew abuse in her name but also said she appreciates the genuine fans who have supported her, the team and the organization.

"As far as people that have used me to demonstrate racist rhetoric or hate or discrimination, that's not something I stand for," Clark said. "That's never been something I've stood for. For those of you that know me, you know that's not what I'm about. It's not how I was raised, so that's really disappointing when people do that.

"I think it kind of gets into this larger discussion in mainstream sports of what people go through. I think just recently I saw Coco Gauff came out and kind of talked about her experience as well. So anytime I see something like that, [it] makes me upset, makes me sad, makes me really disappointed. Because that's not who I am. It's not what I'm about."

Retaining Mitchell, who is an unrestricted free agent after setting the WNBA single-season scoring record, is the top priority for the Fever, but she made it clear that on-court, basketball-related factors won't be the only influence on her decision. Mitchell has played all nine seasons with Indiana after being the No. 2 pick in the 2018 draft.

"For my teammates, obviously, there's a lot of really great things that come with playing here, too," Clark said. "And as far as Kelsey and our future with her, with the organization, she knows how much I love her, and we've talked since the season has ended. And there's nobody I would want to share the backcourt with other than her.

"I know this organization is, we're going to work our butt off to get her back. We're going to recruit her as hard as we can. Every player that is signed to a contract is going to recruit her as hard as we can. We need her. We love her.

"I hope for the rest of my career I get to play alongside her," Clark said.

Mitchell isn't the first player to voice her frustration with fans, particularly those associated with Indiana who crossed the line from critical to abusive. A'ja Wilson of the Aces got into an altercation with a fan during Game 2 of the postseason opening round inside Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Aces teammate Jackie Young took issue with a pair of fans sitting courtside in Indiana in August. None of those involved were found to have violated the league's fan code of conduct. Mercury forward Alyssa Thomas said she received death threats and was called racial slurs after receiving a one-game suspension for making contact with Clark's throat with her first.

General manager Amber Cox said last week that "the attacks on our fanbases have no basis in reality, and they need to stop."

Former Fever player Brianna Turner, who serves as treasurer of the Women's National Basketball Players Association, disagreed, posting on social media, "This is an unequivocally false statement."

Clark said she doesn't remember the last time she has checked her direct messages on social media, specifically to avoid all of the bitter talk.

"I just try to block out the noise the best I can," Clark said. "Obviously, I've been under this microscope with the lights bright for six years now. So you kind of figure out how to navigate it. That doesn't mean everything's easy for me. That doesn't mean there aren't moments that are hard. And that goes the same [for] players in this league, that doesn't make it easy for them. It doesn't mean that there aren't hard days. But, obviously, the WNBA has grown so much, and there's more and more eyeballs. I think for the real fans that do show up and do support and do respect, I applaud you. And there are a lot of you, and that's not just here in Indianapolis. That's across the league.

"I think there's certainly a line, and that can't be crossed," she added. "I think any of us, and any person in their right mind, know that there's certain rhetoric that's just not OK, and that's not something I've ever stood for. But at the same time, there are a lot of really great fans and a lot of fans that I really truly enjoy getting to play in front of and I'm really thankful for. And I thank them for coming out. They made it a great season and were loud every single night.

"But for me, I think just I do the best I can to block it out, block out the noise, and try to limit my time on social media the best I can."

stories.headline: Harry Kane interest in MLS 'fulfilment of a dream' - commissioner
stories.summary: MLS commissioner Don Garber would love Harry Kane to follow Lionel Messi across the pond and says the England skipper's interest helps fulfil a dream that Sir David Beckham kept alive.
stories.body:
MLS commissioner Don Garber would love Harry Kane to follow Lionel Messi across the pond and says the England skipper's interest helps fulfil a dream that Sir David Beckham kept alive.

The 33-year-old is in the running for the Ballon d'Or having scored 73 goals for club and country in a season that saw the striker win the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich before World Cup bronze.

Kane shows no signs of slowing and he marked his record-equalling 125th England appearance by extending his international goal tally to 91 in Tuesday's 3-0 Nations League win against Czechia.

The striker scored six goals across a four-match camp that began with him revealing his interest in eventually moving to MLS as the striker spoke about his dreams of being an NFL kicker.

"I'd love for him to do that," commissioner Garber said. "I think, for me, it is the fulfilment of the dream that we had to build a proper soccer league that would drive a soccer nation. That sounds colloquial but actually we have that written down.

"We wanted to create something that would have the Harry Kanes of the world say 'I'd kind of like to play in MLS.' And I think Messi proved that.

"That was a competitive process, working to ensure that we had a dynamic that would be better than going back to Barca, working a dynamic that would not have him want to play in Saudi Arabia.

"Play in Miami, have them be able to build a new stadium and have him set records and be an MVP, and then have an unbelievable goodbye [this week] from his international career."

Garber welcomes Kane's keenness to move to MLS and is eternally grateful to another England captain as he prepares to step down from the post of commissioner he has held since 1999.

Beckham's move to LA Galaxy acted as the catalyst for the league's growth, which only accelerated when the former midfielder helped form Inter Miami and sign Argentina great Messi in 2023.

"I don't think I would say one is more important than the other," Garber said of the star duo's impact.

"David put this league on the path to credibility and respect. In the prime of his career, he came to LA.

"He came into Major League Soccer and showed the world that this league can be competitive, it could be respected, it could be fun, it could have great players.

"It attracted [Thierry] Henry and many, many other players right after that, so without David there's probably no Major League Soccer.

"That being said, Major League Soccer would not be the global phenomenon and not be sort of on the hearts and minds of just about anybody in the world without Leo Messi."

Garber will become chairman at the turn of the year and is proud of his legacy with MLS, which was founded as part of the bid to hold the 1994 World Cup in a country that has just co-hosted the largest edition of the tournament.

The 68-year-old says they have made the planet's "biggest commercial market for the sport" during that time and is excited to see how they build on firm foundations.

"We just went from a country road, now we're getting onto the highway," Garber told the Press Association. "And we've got to get better.

"We have to have a league that is more competitive, that has an ability to get into the Club World Cup and win games. Miami won one.

"Not just be there but have people think that an MLS team can compete against other clubs in the world."

stories.headline: When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races
stories.summary: With an 84-point lead in the drivers' standings, it is looking increasingly likely that Kimi Antonelli will be crowned F1's youngest world champion in the next two months.
stories.body:
With an 84-point lead in the drivers' standings, it is looking increasingly likely that Kimi Antonelli will be crowned F1's youngest world champion in the next two months.

Determining when and where that coronation will likely take place is much harder to say, not least because there are still question marks over how many races remain in the F1 calendar.

Antonelli's closest competitor, Mercedes teammate George Russell, saw his title chances take a critical blow when he retired from Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia with an engine failure, and a related grid penalty at this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix will make his job tougher still.

Meanwhile, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc, Lando Norris and Max Verstappen all remain in mathematical contention for this year's championship, but face even tougher routes to the title than Russell due to their greater points deficits.

When could Antonelli win his first title?
In theory, the earliest Antonelli could seal the title is at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin later this month. In order to do so, he would need to grow his gap over Russell by 42 points in two race weekends, while outscoring Lewis Hamilton in third place by 20 points.

- Singapore Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch

- Valtteri Bottas cycles 400km from Malaysia to Singapore

- F1 cars to get software update after Malaysia 'bug'

Even with extra points on offer at the sprint race in Singapore this weekend, such a scenario would likely require victories for Antonelli and further retirements for Russell, while ensuring Hamilton is not in the fight for second place on the podium behind Antonelli. In addition, an Austin crowning would require Antonelli to make sure he is not outscored by three points by Leclerc, and six points by both Norris and Verstappen.

What does Antonelli need to claim the title?
Perhaps the easiest way to look at Antonelli's title run-in is that he needs to score 100 points over the remaining races to ensure he ends up as champion -- regardless of what any of his rivals manage.

With seven grands prix and a sprint race currently scheduled on the calendar, that route could be achieved with multiple different result combinations -- but for ease of an example, third place at every remaining race would comfortably see Antonelli over the line even if Russell wins at all seven grands prix and the sprint.

F1's rules state that if multiple drivers are tied on points, a countback of victories will decide who emerges on top. If the number of victories are also even, it then goes to second places, third places, fourth place, and so on. Currently, Antonelli has eight victories to Russell's three, although Russell has four second places to Antonelli's three. It's unlikely those countbacks will come into play, but it's why, currently, Antonelli needs 100 points rather than 99 to put the title entirely beyond Russell's grasp.

But how many races are actually left?
The situation is further complicated by question marks hanging over the final two races of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. F1 has made clear that it intends to finish the season as scheduled, but the ongoing war between the United States and Iran has the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

The same conflict led the cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in April, while Bahrain took the unusual approach of hosting its round 4,000 miles away from the island kingdom in Malaysia last weekend.

If Qatar and Abu Dhabi are also cancelled, F1's contingency plan is to host the final round of the season in Imola. Such a scenario would remove 25 of the potential points on offer, meaning Antonelli would only need 75 points between now and the end of the season to be crowned champion. Austin would still be the earliest round at which he could clinch the title, but it would come with a more achievable target of outscoring Russell by 17 points across the Singapore and U.S. race weekends rather than 42.

stories.headline: Mikel Arteta: 'I still have the scar' from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat
stories.summary: Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta has said he still has a "scar" from Arsenal's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in May.

The Spaniard, whose new four-year contract at the Emirates was announced on Wednesday, took the club to their first Champions League final for 20 years last season but saw his team defeated on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Echoing the words of the last man to take them to the brink of elite European glory -- Arsène Wenger, who previously said that "every defeat is a scar in your heart" -- Arteta told The Athletic: "I still have the scar, like Arsène says.

"I still have that poison in my veins. It has to stay there because that's when you learn and that probably is going to be a massive driver for me and everybody."

Looking towards the future, Arteta added that he was excited for a number of different aspects of the club's growth.

"Globally, with our supporters? Great. How are we going to build the next three squads? Great. How the rules of the game are going to change us, and how we're going to stay ahead of that to take advantage? Great," he said.

"But this is going to happen if every single day we look after what we built. We make it a little bit better, like software that is upgrading and upgrading. When can it stop is infinite."

He added: "It feels like it's still a lot to do, and it's just the beginning."

Arteta has, however, already managed to do something no Arsenal manager had achieved for 22 years: win a league title.

"It wasn't just a trophy. It was a moment that we're going to remember for the rest of our lives," he said.

Asked what game from his Arsenal tenure he would relive, the 44-year-old chose the controversial 1-0 win over West Ham which put the Gunners on the brink of returning to the top of the perch.

"This is football elevated to its best version, when a journey, a moment that can change so many people's lives, goes one way or the other," he said. "You just pray because you know if it goes the wrong side, probably it's gone again.

"That day when I went home, I said, 'We're going to be champions. It is our year. This has happened for a reason, and we're going to get it done.'"

Arsenal return from the international break in Saturday's early kickoff against Leeds United at the Emirates, looking to return to the top of the table ahead of Manchester City's trip to Liverpool on Sunday.

stories.headline: Saints trade ruckman to Cats, chase on for star Swan
stories.summary: Geelong have brokered a trade for St Kilda ruckman Rowan Marshall, further depleting the Cats' draft stocks as Swans defender Nick Blakey eyes a move.
stories.body:
St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No. 14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

Cats football boss Andrew Mackie on Monday indicated an unwillingness to part with their first-round pick for Marshall after the Saints asked for a player to be attached to the trade.

St Kilda football boss Lenny Hayes hailed the fair return for Marshall, who has played 177 AFL games since being a rookie pick at age 21.

"We are pleased to have achieved (adequate compensation) by bringing in another first round selection, alongside our existing pick at eight," Hayes said.

Geelong needed to bolster their ruck stocks, with Rhys Stanley retiring and 21-year-old Mitchell Edwards still finding his feet at the level.

The Cats are among five clubs eyeing Nick Blakey as the Swans defender tests the water for a possible trade.

The 2024 All-Australian was one of five players who served a club-imposed ban through the AFL finals for breaching the club's behavioural standards at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne.

The 26-year-old has since been linked to a move despite being signed to Sydney until 2031.

Swans list boss Chris Keane said the club had not been told Blakey was meeting with rival clubs this week, but remained in talks with his manager Robbie D'Orazio.

"As we sit here right now, these are all hypotheticals," he told Trade Radio.

"It's certainly not something we've actively pursued, and we feel confident that he could walk back into our footy club.

"But given the calibre of player that he is, and the fact that he is contracted for five more years, we feel like making any deal happen would be significantly challenging."

Blakey's preferred option is reportedly Geelong, but the Cats have limited draft capital after executing trades for Marshall and Essendon's Jordan Ridley.

North Melbourne have expressed interest for Blakey, whose father John played in the Kangaroos' 1996 and 1999 premierships across 224 club games.

Essendon are another suitor, with Blakey's former mentors Mark McVeigh and John Longmire joining the club and the Bombers boasting salary cap room following the exits of Zach Merrett and Ridley.

"We haven't had any indication off Nick's management that he's looking to leave Sydney," Essendon list boss Matt Rosa told Trade Radio.

"But certainly we've had some discussions internally and we'll continue to do that."

Blakey has reportedly already met with Gold Coast coach Damien Hardwick, while St Kilda are also expected to make contact.

Any trade for Blakey would likely need to be approved by a club board, given the ongoing police investigation into an alleged sexual assault at the hotel.

Swans vice-captain Isaac Heeney, star midfielder Chad Warner, tagger James Jordon and Blakey were interviewed by police but no charges have been laid.

Riley Bice, another Swan banned for round 24 and the finals campaign, is not being investigated.

In other developments, young Hawk Aidan Schubert has agreed to be traded to Gold Coast in a separate deal that is expected to allow Ben King join Hawthorn as a free agent.

The Suns' 72-hour window to match the Hawks' offer for King or accept compensation, likely pick No. 7 in the draft, ends at 4.15pm (AEDT) on Friday.

The Western Bulldogs are yet to file free agency paperwork for Port Adelaide's Zak Butters ahead of Friday afternoon's deadline.

Port can accept draft compensation, which would currently deliver pick No.5, or match the Bulldogs' offer and force a trade.

The trade period closes on Wednesday evening.

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey player buzz: Injuries to monitor and players to add this week
stories.summary: Fantasy hockey guide to the headlines around the NHL, including injuries to monitor and players to add.
stories.body:
We're only a few days into 2026-27 and teams around the league are already making headlines of both a positive and negative nature. Alex Ovechkin is calling it a career! Dylan Larkin is actually playing! Connor Hellebuyck is nowhere to be found! So let's take our first dive into this freshly-chlorinated pool of NHL news, which is heavily peppered with injury and goaltending items, with our goggles focused on any potential fantasy fallout.

Note: We're excluding ever-evolving injury situations that involve players currently listed as day-to-day, including Jake Sanderson, Mikhail Sergachev, Victor Olofsson, Josh Morrissey etc. Keep a close eye on your player news feed for those pertinent updates.

See more: Rankings | Projections | Mock Draft Lobby

Draft guide | Cheat sheet | October preview | Sign up

Florida Panthers

Aleksander Barkov (knee) isn't brutally hurt after all. First there was concern Barkov might miss most, if not all, of the regular season after doing just that because of a knee injury in 2025-26. No wonder hockey fans across North America exhaled when hearing one of the game's elite centers was then projected to return in 10 to 12 weeks, which was quickly reduced to eight-ish weeks, then more like six. At this rate, we'll see the Panther back on the ice next Tuesday (I'm being facetious). All considered, a positive report all around.

In less pleasant news, we're still awaiting an update on Brad Marchand after the winger slammed his knee hard into a goal post and left the ice without putting an ounce of weight on that leg. It looked bad. Fingers crossed Marchand isn't out long term, but I wouldn't heighten my hopes.

Advice: Place Barkov on IR and wait it out. I'd suggest picking up substitute top center Sam Bennett instead, but he's already largely spoken for in ESPN Fantasy leagues. As for Marchand, get ready to drop him outright if the news is as bad as all that. We should know in a day or two.

Colorado Avalanche

Mackenzie Blackwood is Jared Bednar's top choice in Colorado. We know this because the Avalanche's head coach has started the younger netminder instead of Scott Wedgewood in three straight games to open 2026-27. Which means we very well might not see much of Wedgewood outside of back-to-back situations, of which the Avs only have three this month. Of course, Blackwood can fall hurt or hit a rough patch, but we can't ignore Bednar's preferred approach from the onset.

Advice: Never mind his outstanding numbers from 2025-26, re-think relying on Wedgewood as a prominent No. 1 or No. 2 fantasy netminder this campaign. He might not play that much. Don't wait too long before swapping out the veteran for a more active goalie with perhaps a lesser team. Banking on Wedgewood eventually taking over once more could prove rather costly.

Winnipeg Jets

Connor who? While the former Hart/Vezina winner remains suspended, the Jets' active No. 1 is quickly enamoring himself to Winnipeg hockey fans. After a mediocre debut against the Bruins, Stuart Skinner is two-for-two, allowing just a pair of goals against the Red Wings and -- more impressively -- the mighty Avalanche. He looks sharp. It's worth remembering that, when at his best, this is a netminder capable of taking his team to consecutive Stanley Cup Finals.

Regardless of when Kevin Cheveldayoff trades Connor Hellebuyck, and to where, the Jets' general manager shouldn't feel as hard-pressed to get a top-notch goalie in return. Not when Skinner is performing this astutely behind a bunch of skaters who are producing themselves (see: Kyle Connor).

Advice: If at all unsatisfied with your fantasy goaltending, pick up Skinner while he's performing at the top of his game. As for Hellebuyck, keep him tucked on IR until as long as reasonably possible. Many oddsmakers still favor the suspended netminder to win the Vezina. Meaning there's a sense this standoff in Winnipeg might be resolved sooner rather than later.

Philadelphia Flyers
Michael Bunting is a Flyer. Not a jaw-dropping move, by any extent, but one that could pay out some short-term fantasy dividends. Frustrated with his club's start, and for good reason, Rick Tocchet can be counted on to jostle up his top six ahead of Thursday's contest in Ottawa. A group that might include the winger just signed to a one-year, $1.2-million deal. If only until Philly's more dynamite forwards get going. While Bunting isn't ever going to eclipse 60 points again, he has the wherewithal to put up a quick bunch in making a good first impression.

Advice: Add Bunting in deeper leagues in place of an injured skater expected back in the next two to three weeks. Edmonton's Zach Hyman, for example.

Edmonton Oilers
Devon Levi is the No. 1 netminder for the Oilers. Following a circus of a game in which he surrendered seven and still won in Vancouver, the 24-year-old has been better-than-solid in allowing three total goals through two victories against Seattle and Anaheim. Considering how poorly Tristan Jarry faired in the Oilers' opener, we can expect coach Mike Babcock to run with the younger netminder for the foreseeable future. At least until he struggles himself or Frederik Andersen (knee) is ready to return.

Advice: How desperate are you between the pipes? If more than less, and carry a fairly strong fantasy stomach, Levi could be worth a flier. Sure, Edmonton's defensive play consistently remains a work-in-progress, but this team is also going to score a ton. Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard already have 32 points combined through only four contests. Levi will be offered ample opportunity to win plenty of games.

New York Islanders

According to coach Pete DeBoer, Mathew Barzal (knee inflammation) is expected to return to skating Thursday. If all goes well, we might anticipate the forward's return to competitive play Saturday against the Lightning, or next Tuesday versus the Canucks (Thursday's tilt with the Blackhawks feels premature). Once again projected to lead the Islanders in production -- heavy on the assists -- Barzal remains available in about a third of ESPN Fantasy leagues.

Advice: After missing most of 2024-25, the ongoing knee issue is a bother. Still, Barzal played all but one game this past season, accumulating 72 points. This early, he's worth the health gamble if you need to replace another injured, or unpromising, skater on your fantasy roster.

Ottawa Senators

Linus Ullmark is "fine". At least that's the latest word from head coach Travis Green after the goalie was recently tackled by Bruins forward JJ Peterka. Okay. So, until we receive further notice, it feels reasonable enough to expect Ottawa's No. 1 to start against the Flyers in the team's home opener Thursday. If, however, Green instead opts to go with Samuel Ersson for a second straight game, I assure you Ullmark isn't entirely fine at all.

Advice: Keep a grip on Ullmark if/until the situation seems more grim. No matter what, there are better fantasy options around the league than Ersson.

Pittsburgh Penguins

Bryan Rust is back in business. Wrapping up his recovery from an upper-body injury through the Penguins' first three games, Rust celebrated his 2026-27 debut with three shots, a goal, and nearly 20 minutes of ice time. Splitting minutes between the Penguins third unit, and top line with Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell, the consistent shooter is expected to, once again, settle into the latter role. When fit and active, Rust serves as a well-balanced -- the extra blocked shots never hurt -- and underrated fantasy performer.

Advice: Grab Rust in all but the shallowest of leagues while tempering your fantasy expectations of Hendrix Lapierre. Losing his spot on the top line to the veteran winger, the Pittsburgh newbie falls to the third unit alongside Ben Kindel and Ville Koivunen.

stories.headline: Fantasy basketball: Category league draft tiers
stories.summary: Eric Moody groups players into tiers by each position for category-based leagues.
stories.body:
Category leagues require a different approach than points leagues. Volume still matters, but it isn't everything. Steals and blocks are harder to find, while 3-pointers can be concentrated among certain types of players. Field goal percentage, free throw percentage and turnovers can quietly swing a league over the course of a season.

That can change how players should be valued.

A guard who gives you steals, 3-pointers and strong percentages can be more valuable than a higher-scoring player who hurts you elsewhere. A center who blocks shots without wrecking your free throw percentage can give you a major advantage. A forward who provides assists can help solve a shortage in a category that is harder to address at that position.

Our recent 10-team roto mock showed how that can play out. Four point guards went in the first round, while no small forwards were selected. Then Cooper Flagg, Scottie Barnes and Amen Thompson went with three of the first four picks of Round 2. Point guard became a focus again in Round 3, when James Harden, Jalen Brunson, Josh Giddey, LaMelo Ball, Jamal Murray and Stephen Curry all came off the board in a seven-pick span.

Derrick White also went 17th overall, which makes sense given how difficult his combination of 3s, assists, steals and blocks is to replace at shooting guard. Power forward showed one of the clearest positional drop-offs, while center remained deep enough that useful rebounders and shot-blockers were still available well into the middle rounds.

That's where tiers become useful.

I've separated players by their default position, even if they qualify at multiple spots. The rankings show how I value the players in a neutral build. The tiers show where the player pool changes. Once the draft starts, what you already have should influence what comes next.

The goal isn't simply to draft the highest-ranked player every round. It's to know from round to round what your team does well, where it is vulnerable and when a category or position is about to become much harder to draft.

The rankings tell you who I like. The tiers tell you when you need to act. Your roster tells you who fits best.

To see points league draft tiers, click here.

See more: Sign up | Rankings | Projections | Mock Draft Lobby

Draft guide | 'Do not draft' list | Which league is right for you?

Point guards

Thoughts on PGs

Gilgeous-Alexander and Doncic are the clear top two, but they give category managers very different foundations. Gilgeous-Alexander is projected for 31.3 PPG while shooting 53.6% from the field and 88.3% from the line, with 1.7 SPG and only 2.3 turnovers a game. You get elite scoring without taking a major hit elsewhere. Doncic gives you even more volume in points, 3s, rebounds and assists, but his projected 78.3% free throw shooting and 4.0 turnover average have to be managed.
Maxey, Cunningham and Haliburton form the next tier. Haliburton stands out because of how efficiently he provides assists. He's projected for 9.9 per game with just 1.9 turnovers while also averaging 2.9 3-pointers. That combination is hard to find later.
Murray, Ball and Harden remain strong options, but there is a meaningful drop after the first five point guards. Ball helps in assists, 3s and rebounds, while Harden still brings high-end playmaking and free throw production.
Curry is especially valuable in categories because his 3-point volume and free throw percentage can swing two categories. He doesn't need the same rebound or assist totals as other guards to return high-end value.
Giddey has a completely different profile. His rebounding and assists from the point guard spot make it easier to chase scoring, 3s or defensive stats elsewhere.
Young remains one of the league's best sources of assists, 3-pointers and free throw production, but the field goal percentage and turnovers come with a cost. He fits better on teams that can absorb those weaknesses.
As you move deeper into the position, focus more on what category you still need. Assists remain available, but the later options are more likely to hurt you in percentages, turnovers or scoring.

The last word: Point guard is deep enough to wait on if you miss the elite options.

Shooting guard

Thoughts on SGs

Edwards and Mitchell sit comfortably at the top because both give you excellent scoring and 3-point volume without creating an obvious weakness elsewhere.
White deserves his own tier. He's projected for 2.9 3-pointers, 5.3 APG, 1.1 SPG and 1.2 BPG. The blocks separate him from the rest of the position. Getting that production from a guard means you don't have to chase as much shot-blocking from your bigs.
Alexander-Walker, Daniels and Bane get to their value in different ways. Bane gives you scoring, 3s and strong free throw shooting. Alexander-Walker adds 3-point shooting and defensive production. Daniels is the specialist of the group, with a projected 2.0 SPG, 6.5 RPG and 5.6 APG.
Daniels is also a good example of why category leagues are different. His 0.4 projected 3s per game and 61.7% free throw shooting are clear weaknesses, but the steals can be valuable enough to offset them depending on your build.
Reaves and Dejounte Murray both contribute across several counting categories. Reaves gives you scoring, assists and efficiency, while Murray adds assists, rebounds and steals.
Sheppard's projected 1.5 SPG and 0.7 BPG give him value even if his offensive role remains modest.
Wallace fits a similar mold. He doesn't need a huge offensive role if he can contribute steals, keep turnovers low and make enough 3s.

The last word: Scoring and 3-pointers are easier to replace at shooting guard. Steals, blocks and clean percentages are not.

Small forwards

Thoughts on SFs

Barnes, Thompson, Flagg and Leonard make up an impressive first tier, but they help category teams in different ways.
Barnes is projected for 7.7 RPG, 6.0 APG, 1.4 SPG and 1.3 BPG. The assists and blocks are especially valuable because both are harder to find from a small forward. Thompson has a very different profile. 3-pointers are not a strength, but his field goal percentage, rebounding and defensive production can make up for it. He fits especially well if you already have enough shooting.
Flagg can contribute across several categories without one glaring weakness shaping the rest of your build. That makes him easier to fit into different types of teams.
Leonard remains one of the easiest players to fit into a category build when healthy. He's projected to shoot 51.0% from the field and 87.9% from the line while adding 2.3 3s and 1.7 SPG. The issue is availability, not fit.
Bridges sits in his own tier because he contributes across the board without hurting you in many areas. He also fits easily next to almost any early-round core. Knueppel, Porter and Murphy give you ways to add 3-point shooting without sacrificing the rest of the box score.
Buzelis is projected for 2.3 3-pointers and 1.6 BPG. That's a rare combination from a wing and gives him more category value than his scoring alone suggests. Later in the draft, small forward becomes more about fit. Some players give you 3s. Others help with steals, rebounds or efficiency.

The last word: The position has enough depth that you don't need to force it just because you haven't filled the spot yet.

Power forwards

Thoughts on PFs

Tatum and Johnson sit at the top, and Johnson's category profile is unusual for a power forward.
Johnson is projected for 23.0 PPG, 10.6 RPG and 7.9 APG. The assists are the key. Getting nearly eight per game from a power forward reduces how much playmaking you need from your guards.
Tatum gives you a more traditional elite forward profile with scoring, 3s, rebounds and great free throw shooting. He fits easily into a balanced build because there isn't one category you immediately need to fix.
Antetokounmpo stands alone in Tier 2 because his profile comes with a clear tradeoff. His projected 32.1 PPG, 11.4 RPG, 6.3 APG and elite field goal percentage can dominate several categories, but the projected 65.0% free throw shooting can do the opposite.
Drafting Antetokounmpo doesn't automatically mean punting free throws, but you need a plan. You can try to offset the free throw weakness with strong shooters elsewhere or accept it and build around Antetokounmpo' strengths.
Siakam, Mobley and Durant are easier to fit into balanced builds. Mobley helps with field goal percentage, rebounds and blocks. Durant can anchor both percentages while adding scoring and 3-pointers. Siakam contributes scoring, rebounds and assists without forcing your roster in one direction.
Markkanen and Williams are where the position gets thin. Williams is No. 35 in the overall category rankings, while the next power forward, Banchero, doesn't appear until No. 75. That's a major drop in projected value.
After that, the position becomes more roster-dependent. Murray can help with 3s and defensive stats. Collins is useful for field goal percentage and rebounds. Camara becomes more appealing when steals are a need.

The last word: Power forward has the biggest positional cliff in the player pool. If you wait too long, the options at the position can drop off quickly.

Centers

Thoughts on Cs

Jokic and Wembanyama belong together at the top, but they build teams in very different ways.
Jokic is projected for 28.3 PPG, 12.7 RPG and 10.1 APG while shooting 57.5% from the field. The assists are especially valuable because you're getting point-guard-level playmaking from your center spot.
Wembanyama gives you something even harder to replace: 3.5 projected BPG. He also projects for averages of 26.3 PPG, 12.2 RPG and 2.2 3s, so you aren't sacrificing offense to get elite shot-blocking. If you draft Wembanyama, you can spend later picks chasing other categories instead of worrying about blocks.
Davis, Adebayo and Towns form another strong tier. Davis is projected for 11.4 RPG, 2.1 BPG and 53.8% shooting from the field. His per-game profile can finish much higher if he stays healthy.
Duren, Sengun and Sabonis give you different paths at the position. Duren helps with rebounds and field goal percentage. Sengun and Sabonis stand out because of the assists they provide at center.
Sabonis is projected for 13.6 RPG and 6.8 APG while shooting 58.7% from the field. That makes him especially useful if you don't want all of your playmaking coming from guards.
Reid has a less traditional center profile. His combination of 3s, rebounds and defensive stats makes him easier to pair with a paint-bound big who doesn't stretch the floor.
Clingan, Okongwu and Kessler are where roster fit matters more. Clingan gives you rebounds, blocks and some 3-point production. Okongwu contributes 3s along with steals and blocks. Kessler gives you elite rebounds and blocks, but the free throw percentage can be a problem.
If you're already punting free throw percentage, Kessler's value rises. If you're trying to stay competitive in all nine categories, he's harder to fit.
Holmgren, Sarr and Jackson give you another path because they can provide blocks while still contributing from the perimeter.
Embiid is the ultimate risk-reward option. His per-game production belongs several tiers higher, but his availability makes him much harder to trust.

The last word: Center gives you more flexibility than any other position if you miss the elite options. Rebounds, blocks and field goal percentage remain available later, but the later choices usually come with a tradeoff.

Final thoughts

The biggest mistake in a category draft is treating the board like a straight ranking exercise.

Your first few picks start to shape your team. Draft Antetokounmpo and free throw percentage becomes a concern. Take Doncic and you may want to protect field goal percentage and turnovers. Land Wembanyama and blocks become much less urgent.

That doesn't mean you should start punting categories after two rounds. You just need to know where your team is strong, where it's weak and what you can afford to give up.

That's why a player ranked 45th can be a better pick for your team than someone ranked 35th. If you already have plenty of scoring and 3-pointers but need steals, Dyson Daniels can make more sense than another scorer.

Point guard is deep. Derrick White is an important decision point at shooting guard. Small forward has enough depth that you don't need to force it. Power forward has the biggest drop-off. Center still offers plenty of rebounds, blocks and field goal percentage later.

The rankings tell you who I like. The tiers tell you when you need to act. Your roster tells you who fits best.

stories.headline: Mourinho jokes he'll be lucky to still be around when Man City case ends
stories.summary: Real Madrid coach José Mourinho joked that he'll be lucky to still be around to see the final verdict in the Premier League's case against Manchester City.
stories.body:
Real Madrid coach José Mourinho joked that he'll be lucky to still be around to see the final verdict in the Premier League's case against Manchester City.

An independent commission's verdict published last week found City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules. It detailed how City arranged "sham" commercial deals to inflate revenues and reduce costs by £900 million ($1.2b billion) during a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

- What's next for Man City? Appeals, possible punishments, how long it could take

- Haaland: City must 'stay positive' amid PL case

- Man City's Maresca 'trusts the club completely'

The verdict came 21 months after the culmination of a 12-week hearing, following an investigative process that dates back to 2019.

However, City have appealed the verdict and say they have "irrefutable evidence" of their innocence.

And Mourinho, who led Manchester United to second place in the Premier League behind City in 2017-18, said he is not holding his breath waiting for the case to come to its conclusion.

"I would rather laugh about ‌it," ⁠Mourinho said of the case during an interview with Italian publication Corriere dello Sport. "I think we will eventually get an ending, but we are both in our 60s and we'll need ​to be lucky ​enough to still ⁠be around when the final verdict arrives.

"There will be a verdict, then appeals, then more appeals."

Mourinho has previously said that he may still receive a winners' medal if City are stripped of the prize.

The Premier League said that City's appeal to an independent appeal board "will remain private and confidential until publication of the outcome is permitted."

Fines, points deductions and other sporting sanctions are among "a broad discretion" of sanctions available to the commission, the Premier League also said.

ESPN has reported that a timeframe is in place for City's fate to be resolved by the end of this season.

But City could yet take the case beyond sporting regulatory bodies to the High Court in the United Kingdom if the appeal fails and City can prove serious irregularities in the Premier League's disciplinary process.

Information from ESPN's Mark Ogden was used in this report.

stories.headline: Silva rises in P4P women's top 10, making most of golden opportunity
stories.summary: After winning UFC women's flyweight title, Silva rises in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
The women's flyweight division might be the most stacked weight class in the UFC, and Natalia Silva wears the gold.

Silva was too fast, too precise and too elusive for Wang Cong in the UFC 332 main event on Saturday, and as a result, the 29-year-old from Brazil captured the vacant 125-pound title. She moves up one position to No. 4 in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

Silva is one of seven flyweights in the women's top 10. The division with the next most pound-for-pound elites is lightweight, with three fighters in the men's rankings.

The top two fighters on the women's list are Valentina Shevchenko, who vacated the UFC title last month while healing shoulder and back injuries, and Zhang Weili, a two-time former strawweight titlist who last fought at flyweight, in an unsuccessful challenge of Shevchenko in November.

Aside from Silva, there are three other UFC flyweights in the top 10 (Alexa Grasso, Manon Fiorot and Erin Blanchfield), and the rankings also include PFL 125-pounder Dakota Ditcheva.

UFC women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison has been missing from these rankings for the past few months because, with no fights since June 2025, she is ineligible. But Harrison will return from neck surgery to defend her title against former two-division champion and consensus GOAT Amanda Nunes at UFC 334 on Nov. 14.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Oct. 7. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which Natalia Silva captured by beating Wang Cong at UFC 332. When Shevchenko is healed up, she'll be looking to take back the belt.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 21-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Wang Cong, Oct. 3

Next: TBA

Silva was looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324. And now she has fulfilled that expectation, beating Wang at UFC 332 to win the belt vacated by injured Valentina Shevchenko. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

5. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Previous ranking: 4

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her upcoming bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Natalia Silva; 5. Cris Cyborg; 6. Alexa Grasso; 7. Manon Fiorot; 8. Dakota Ditcheva; 9. Erin Blanchfield; 10. Tatiana Suarez.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (38) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch at UFC 331. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight on the White House lawn. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from a challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

stories.headline: Clark to consider Fever roster before signing new 'EPIC' deal
stories.summary: Caitlin Clark said she will consider the Fever's roster before signing a new contract through the new "EPIC" provision in the latest collective bargaining agreement.
stories.body:
Caitlin Clark is now eligible for the new "EPIC" (Exceptional Performance on Initial Contract) provision included in the latest collective bargaining agreement that allows players to renegotiate the fourth year of their rookie deals and sign three-year extensions. The three-time All-Star, 2024 Rookie of the Year and 2024 first-team All-WNBA selection, however, isn't necessarily looking to sign the extension.

"We have to think about things with the cap," Clark said, "and what we're going to need and who we're going to need to sign and what value they bring to the team.

"Not saying I'm going to sign it or not sign it. I think it's just kind of figuring out the way we need to construct our roster. No matter what, I'm gonna be here. I just want to do what's best for the team and make sure we have the opportunity to be able to win championships. Like, that's my main goal."

Clark could sign for the projected max of $1.3 million in 2027 and the projected supermax of $1.7 million in 2028, which would be the first year of her extended deal. Under the EPIC provision, qualifying players can earn the max in their fourth year if they were previously named All-WNBA first or second team, or they can earn the supermax if they were named MVP. She finished the season ranked No. 3 in points per game and No. 2 in assists per game.

General manager Amber Cox will have some decisions to make after the Fever fell to the No. 6 seed in the playoffs for a third consecutive season and didn't make it out of the first round. Kelsey Mitchell, Sophie Cunningham, Tyasha Harris and Myisha Hines-Allen are all unrestricted free agents, so there could be some significant changes throughout the roster.

Clark indicated that she intends to have a voice in the room as roster construction is discussed and would be active in recruiting any free agents. She called it a "responsibility" as a leader on the team and believes Aliyah Boston and, hopefully, Mitchell, would be involved too.

"Us and Amber, we always have open dialog about players," Clark said. "You hear rumblings about how players are in the locker room or what they're like to play with and things like that. That's all helpful to the GM or whatever it is. You share those types of things about who you think we can get or whose play style will fit next to whoever it is, and what positions are most important for us to get.

"Those are definitely conversations we have with Amber. At the end of the day, Amber's the GM and she makes the final call, but she certainly asks us our opinion, and wants us to have a voice in that."

stories.headline: George Russell and Kimi Antonelli to run different Mercedes packages at Singapore Grand Prix
stories.summary: Title rivals Kimi Antonelli and George Russell will drive different specifications of Mercedes' Formula 1 car at this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix as the team searches for answers over its lack of performance in Malaysia.
stories.body:
Title rivals Kimi Antonelli and George Russell will drive different specifications of Mercedes' Formula 1 car at this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix as the team searches for answers over its lack of performance in Malaysia.

Antonelli will run the upgraded aerodynamic package that the team debuted last weekend, while Russell will revert to the previous specification that won races in Monza, Madrid and Baku.

The team hopes that running a comparison between the two cars will help it understand why the new package did not perform as expected in Malaysia and allow it to define a longer-term development direction.

Russell is Antonelli's closest rival in this year's drivers' championship, although a power unit failure in Malaysia saw him fall 84 points behind his teammate in the standings.

Russell claims he pushed for the two cars to run different specifications this weekend as soon as it became clear in Malaysia that the new package was not performing.

He said the decision then became a "no-brainer" when his power unit failure on Sunday meant he would be starting from the back of the grid in Singapore due to an engine penalty.

"Actually, I instigated the conversation prior to the race [in Malaysia] on Sunday," Russell said. "So when the failure happened it was kind of a no-brainer because we were 50-50 about it pre-race and I was more in favour to do it, and now it is a total no-brainer."

Russell suspects the lack of performance compared to rivals Red Bull in Malaysia was more track specific than a direct result of the upgrade, but welcomed the opportunity to return to the car specification he won with at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix two weeks ago.

"We're pretty confident it [the lack of performance] is Malaysia specific," he said. "When you look at the pace of Red Bull as well, they clearly overperformed compared to where they've been this season compared to all of the other teams.

"And actually when you look at our pace compared to McLaren and Ferrari it wasn't too dissimilar, it wasn't massively out of bed.

"So with this engine penalty this weekend has just given them a good opportunity to roll back, it's the car that I won in Baku with, so yeah that's it."

The upgrade package is the result of months of development work after Mercedes opted not to keep pace with the updates of its rivals and instead work towards a single significant step for the final third of the season.

The upgrades to the car are far-reaching, including a new floor, rear suspension, and noticeable changes to the upper bodywork of the car, including its engine cover.

- F1 cars to get software update after Malaysia 'bug' to prevent repeat at future races

- Singapore Grand Prix 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions

- Rwanda F1 race: Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen welcome prospect of Africa return as talks gather pace

Antonelli believes the upgrade ultimately has more potential but still requires setup work to unlock it.

"It's just a matter of trying to put the car in the right window and understand it more," he said. "And this weekend, I think, is a good example. It's going to be a good opportunity to see and to compare the two packages, because we know the old one -- we've known it for ages.

"We know how to set up the car around that package, we know it works really well and it's really fast in these kind of tracks.

"And, you know, we really want to understand, on the other hand, this new package and trying to really extract the maximum out of it, because the team has done a tremendous job. They're doing so much work on this new package and it would be just a shame to write it off so early.

"So I feel like I'm quite comfortable on keeping it. And actually, you know, I really want to help the team out to understand it more and to, as I said before, try to extract the potential."

Russell, who has won three races to Antonelli's eight, said via PA, ahead of this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix: "The guy who's performed the best is the guy who's leading the championship.

"If you add up the numbers and the points, I still think I'd be very much in the game in an ordinary season. I still think I'd be on the back foot, but in the game for it to flip very quick.

"When you add up the points from this season that have been lost, you know, I've probably had more failures this year than I've had in the three seasons put together.

"Of course, it's tough to take. If I'm being 100% fair with myself, as I've said before, the performance this season hasn't been strong enough. And it probably would have affected me more if these results have ... Like, who knows if I'd have still been in the fight or not, in a more normal circumstance.

"But obviously the pressure and the momentum, every setback has an impact on that momentum.

"It's been pretty incredible how things have panned out this year. But you've just got to focus on what you can control."
